l4_steps.name: Aggregate crew flight duty period records
l4_steps.input: Published rosters, completed duty reports, ACARS sign-on/sign-off logs
l4_steps.output: Crew duty history dataset; cumulative flight hours register
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥99% within 24 hrs of duty completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing ACARS sign-on/sign-off data during irregular ops causes duty time calculation gaps requiring manual correction in Jeppesen; sync delays post-disruption inflate analyst reconciliation workload by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Extract simulator training completion records
l4_steps.input: Completed simulator session logs; CAE Simfinity session completion events
l4_steps.output: Training currency status per crew member; upcoming expiry alert list
l4_steps.kpi: Training record update latency ≤4 hrs post-session; record accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Third-party simulator vendor API reliability varies — CAE Simfinity batch exports rather than real-time push require overnight reconciliation; discrepancies between carrier records and CAE records require manual adjudication with vendor

l4_steps.name: Collect in-flight LOSA & IOE observation reports
l4_steps.input: Line Operational Safety Audit (LOSA) forms; Initial Operating Experience (IOE) completion records
l4_steps.output: Standardised crew observation reports; threat-and-error management (TEM) scores per crew
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 line observations per crew member per 12-month rolling window; observation form completion rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Check airman availability conflicts with revenue operations — scheduling a standards captain as observer removes a qualified crew member from a revenue flight; subjective scoring inconsistency across check airmen requires periodic inter-rater reliability calibration sessions (FAR Part 121.409)

l4_steps.name: Aggregate customer satisfaction scores by crew assignment
l4_steps.system: Medallia CX Platform / Amadeus Altéa PSS (crew-flight linkage)
l4_steps.input: Post-flight NPS surveys; in-flight service feedback; complaint records
l4_steps.output: Crew-attributed satisfaction scorecard; NPS and complaint rate per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Crew-attributed NPS ≥72; cabin crew complaint rate <0.3 per 1,000 PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Survey response rate <15% limits statistical significance at individual crew level — scores based on <5 responses are flagged as unreliable; Altéa crew-to-flight linkage requires manual reconciliation when irregular ops causes crew substitutions not captured in final manifest

l4_steps.name: Validate recurrent training compliance deadlines
l4_steps.input: Crew training currency records; FAR Part 121.433 compliance calendar; carrier AQP programme schedule
l4_steps.output: Training compliance status matrix; 30/60/90-day expiry alert distribution
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members operating with lapsed recurrent training; ≥30-day advance alert issued for 100% of expiring qualifications
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 recurrent training windows are crew-type specific and vary by AQP approval — Jeppesen qualification rules must be manually updated when FAA approves AQP amendments; last-minute scheduling conflicts (crew illness, irregular ops) cause near-miss compliance breaches requiring emergency simulator slots

l4_steps.name: Review proficiency check results and competency grades
l4_steps.system: CAE Simfinity Training Management / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Completed proficiency check (PC) grade sheets; simulator session recordings; AQP competency unit scores
l4_steps.output: PC pass/fail determination; graded competency assessment per AQP unit; recheck scheduling flag
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt PC pass rate ≥94%; recheck completion within 30 days of initial failure
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent grading standards across check airmen require periodic inter-rater reliability audits — FAA ATOS inspectors have cited grading variance in Part 121 operator evaluations; simulator slot scarcity for MAX-type recurrent events (shared with new-entrant type rating candidates) causes recheck scheduling delays beyond the 30-day window

l4_steps.name: Verify medical certificate currency and fitness-for-duty status
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / CASS (Crew Authorisation & Scheduling System)
l4_steps.input: FAA First Class medical examination reports from AME; crew qualification records
l4_steps.output: Medical currency status flag per crew member; crew legal-to-fly determination
l4_steps.kpi: 100% medical certificate currency verified before scheduling assignment; zero FAR Part 61.23 violations
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA First Class medical certificate validity (12 months under age 40, 6 months over 40) requires proactive scheduling of AME appointments — AME scarcity in crew domicile cities (especially smaller hubs) causes crew members to approach expiry without confirmed exam slots; CASS medical flag propagation to Jeppesen rostering has 2–4 hr latency creating a window for illegal assignment

l4_steps.name: Assess type rating and route qualification currency
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / Amadeus Altéa PSS (crew qualification module)
l4_steps.input: Type rating certificates; route qualification records; recency requirements per FAR Part 121.439
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification matrix; route and fleet assignment eligibility flags
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification matrix accuracy ≥99.9%; zero illegal crew assignments attributable to qualification data error
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-system qualification storage (Altéa holds PSS-level eligibility; Jeppesen holds operational crew management records) creates synchronisation risk — a qualification update applied in one system but not the other can result in illegal assignment; no real-time bidirectional API between Altéa and Jeppesen requires manual reconciliation after each qualification event

l4_steps.name: Compile integrated performance scorecard per crew member
l4_steps.system: AWS Redshift / Tableau (crew performance analytics dashboard)
l4_steps.input: Duty records from Jeppesen; training grades from CAE Simfinity; LOSA scores; CSAT data from Medallia; FOQA exceedance flags
l4_steps.output: Consolidated crew performance scorecard (quarterly); percentile ranking within crew category
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard completion rate 100% within 30 days of quarter-end; data freshness ≤24 hrs from source systems
l4_steps.pain_point: Five-source ETL pipeline (Jeppesen, CAE Simfinity, Medallia, FOQA, ASAP) requires ongoing maintenance — schema changes by any vendor break ingestion pipelines; AWS Redshift refresh latency spikes during post-irregular-ops recovery periods when data volumes are 3–5× normal

l4_steps.name: Review FOQA exceedances and ASAP safety report history
l4_steps.system: FOQA (Flight Operational Quality Assurance platform) / ASAP tracking system
l4_steps.input: FOQA exceedance alert reports; ASAP self-disclosure submissions; ATC incident notifications
l4_steps.output: Safety event summary per crew member; corrective action flags; ASAP ERC review outcomes
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA exceedance rate <2.5 per 1,000 flight hours; ASAP report ERC review cycle ≤14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: ASAP programme confidentiality provisions (FAA MOU requirement) restrict sharing of individual ASAP submissions with HR performance systems — safety managers must deconflict performance use of safety data from ASAP protections to avoid chilling voluntary disclosure; FOQA data volume from 800+ aircraft requires automated triage algorithm to prioritise analyst review

l4_steps.name: Conduct formal performance appraisal interview
l4_steps.input: Compiled performance scorecard; training records summary; safety event history; prior appraisal ratings
l4_steps.output: Signed performance appraisal document; development goals for next period; performance rating
l4_steps.kpi: Appraisal completion rate ≥98% within performance period; crew satisfaction with appraisal process ≥75% (internal survey)
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors has no native integration with Jeppesen Crew Management — crew performance data must be manually exported as CSV and uploaded to SuccessFactors before each appraisal cycle, creating data staleness risk; union CBA provisions (ALPA, AFA contracts) restrict appraisal content, frequency, and the use of ASAP/FOQA data in formal evaluations

l4_steps.name: Initiate Performance Improvement Plan with union review
l4_steps.input: Below-threshold performance appraisal; applicable CBA provisions; HR policy framework
l4_steps.output: Signed PIP document; action timeline with milestone dates; union representative notification
l4_steps.kpi: PIP initiation within 10 business days of appraisal decision; ≥70% PIP completion success rate (crew returns to standard performance)
l4_steps.pain_point: ALPA and AFA CBAs impose strict procedural requirements on PIP content and duration — legal review adds 5–10 business days before issuance; PIP templates must differ by crew category (captain, first officer, flight attendant) due to different contractual language, increasing HR preparation workload

l4_steps.name: Schedule targeted remedial simulator or recurrent training
l4_steps.system: CAE Simfinity (simulator booking) / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: PIP-specified training requirements; simulator capacity calendar; crew availability roster
l4_steps.output: Confirmed simulator training assignment; crew notification; updated Jeppesen training record
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial training scheduled within 21 days of PIP initiation; simulator slot utilisation ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Q4 recurrent training demand surge (driven by anniversary-month training windows clustering in autumn) competes directly with remedial training scheduling — PIP trainees are lower-priority than regulatory recurrent events, causing delays beyond the 21-day target; CAE Simfinity booking API rate limits cause queuing delays during bulk roster update events

l4_steps.name: Monitor PIP milestone progress and conduct gate reviews
l4_steps.input: Completed training results; line observation scores; PIP milestone schedule
l4_steps.output: PIP progress report; pass/continue/escalate/terminate decision per gate
l4_steps.kpi: Gate reviews completed on schedule ≥95%; escalation decision issued within 5 business days of missed milestone
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors milestone alert configuration requires manual setup per PIP — no automated trigger from Jeppesen training completion events; inconsistent documentation standards across fleet types make cross-fleet PIP outcome comparisons unreliable for HR trend analysis

l4_steps.name: Generate FAA/AQP regulatory compliance report
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / AWS S3 (compliance data lake)
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records; training completion data; medical certificate currency; PC results
l4_steps.output: AQP compliance report; ATOS audit evidence package; FAA programme approval data
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory report submission on-time rate 100%; zero FAA violation notices attributable to reporting failures
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121 Subpart Y (AQP) reporting requires carrier-specific competency unit data formats not natively exported by Jeppesen — manual report assembly from three source systems increases error risk during FAA ATOS audit periods; AWS S3 data lake partitioning strategy for crew records requires careful schema governance to support ad-hoc FAA data requests

l4_steps.name: Update crew qualification records in PSS and crew system
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Completed training events; new qualifications issued; medical certificate updates; PIP outcomes
l4_steps.output: Updated qualification eligibility flags in Altéa and Jeppesen; crew scheduling restrictions lifted or applied
l4_steps.kpi: Record update latency ≤4 hrs post-qualification event; dual-system sync accuracy ≥99.99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-system update requirement (Altéa + Jeppesen) with no real-time sync creates a window during which Altéa reflects updated qualification but Jeppesen does not (or vice versa), enabling an illegal crew assignment if a scheduling query is run in the lagging system during the sync gap

l4_steps.name: Archive performance records per regulatory retention policy
l4_steps.input: Performance appraisals; PIP documents; training records; safety event reports; medical records
l4_steps.output: Archived records package; retention schedule compliance confirmation; access control audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Record archival within 5 business days of period close; zero GDPR or FAR Part 121.683 retention violations
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.683 requires training records retention for the duration of employment plus 1 year, while GDPR (applicable to EU crew and EU-operated routes) mandates data minimisation and right-to-erasure — these requirements conflict for international crew records and require per-jurisdiction retention rules not supported by default AWS S3 lifecycle policies
